text: When you design a REST API, it is important to follow some best practices. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints that describe the resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct status codes so clients understand what happened. For example, use 200 for success, 201 for creation, and 404 when a resource is not found. Third, provide good documentation so other developers can learn how to use your API quickly. Finally, think about versioning. As your API grows and changes, versioning helps keep old clients working while you add new features. Following these simple rules will make your API easier to use, maintain, and trust.
